name: Winged eyeliner for tilt

lead: Winged eyeliner extends the line along the upper lashes past the outer corner of the eye. The payoff is a more upturned outer corner, the look of a positive canthal tilt, and a more defined eye shape, visible as soon as it is applied.
It is a long-standing makeup style that looksmaxxing communities discuss as a way to imitate canthal tilt. No published research was found on how it changes perceived eye tilt.

paras: A dark line is drawn along the upper lash line and flicked outward and upward, so the eye is visually extended in that direction. It is done with ordinary pencil or liquid liners, and the wing is typically drawn toward about the end of the eyebrow.
Eyeliner is a standard cosmetic with mainly irritation concerns. Product quality varies by region, and the FDA has described traditional kohl as unsafe because of lead.

angle.text: The wing is drawn outward and upward to suggest an upturned outer eye corner, giving the eyes a more tilted, defined shape as soon as it is applied. It is a standard makeup technique, and no formal studies of its effect on perceived tilt were found.

lead: Winged eyeliner defines the upper lid and extends the line outward to a point about halfway toward the end of the eyebrow. A related style, cat eye, uses a thicker wing that runs along both upper and lower lash lines [1].
In looksmaxxing discussions the wing is mentioned as a cosmetic way to suggest a positive canthal tilt. The sources reviewed contain no studies of how liner affects perceived eye tilt.
infobox: Liquid, pencil, gel, felt-tip and others

paras: Eyeliner is sold as liquid, powder pencil, wax pencil, kohl, gel, cake, shimmer and felt-tip products [1]. Dark lines around the eyes have an ancient history, with Egyptians using materials such as copper ore and antimony [1]. In the 1960s liquid liner produced bold graphic lines associated with designer Mary Quant [1].

timeline.event: Liquid liner creates bold graphic lines in fashion makeup [1].
